title: FERC General Correspondence — Docket P-2652-000: Letter to PacifiCorp acknowledging the 08/19/2026 Dam Safety Inspection of the Bigfork Project, no immediate requirements follow up actions listed; under P-2652.
text:
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
Office of Energy Projects
Division of Dam Safety and Inspections – Portland Regional Office
9/1/2026
In reply refer to:
P-2652
VIA Electronic Mail
Mr. William Shallenberger
Vice President, Renewable Resources
PacifiCorp
Will.Shallenberger@pacificorp.com
Subject: 2026 Dam Safety Inspection Follow-Up, Bigfork Hydroelectric Project
Dear Mr. Shallenberger:
On August 19, 2026, Mr. Kareem Bynoe and Mr. Dennis Hanneman performed an
inspection of the Bigfork Hydroelectric Project, FERC No. 2652. The project features
were inspected and no conditions were found that would require immediate remedial
action to protect the safety of the project.
Bigfork Diversion Dam (FED ID: MT00220) is in Poor condition based on the
National Inventory of Dams (NID) Condition Assessment definitions. Seepage and
evidence of internal erosion have been observed at the right embankment. Based on our
review, PacifiCorp has implemented appropriate interim risk reduction measures
(IRRMs) while remediation planning is under way. We did not observe any conditions
during the inspection that would change this Condition Assessment rating nor warrant the
implementation of additional IRRMs.
The items listed below were discussed with Mr. Zachary Kocaj during the
inspection and will require follow-up actions by PacifiCorp:
1. Decaying vegetation, consisting of a root mass, was observed at the outlet of the
right embankment toe drain. Upon closer inspection, Operations staff were able to
manually remove an approximately 4-foot-long by 2-inch-thick root and debris
mass from the toe drain. The root mass in the toe drain is not an immediate dam
safety concern but does directly influence the toe drain flow measurements and
could lead to inaccurate drain flow readings. In addition, prolonged unaddressed
obstructions to the toe drain could lead to a complete blockage of the drain,
reducing its effectiveness at conveying seepage. PacifiCorp should review the

2
monitoring procedures for the right embankment toe drain and include clearing
debris from the toe drain outlet as a part of the monitoring program before drain
flow readings are recorded.
2. Evidence of woody vegetation growing on the downstream slope of the right
embankment was observed and has the potential to create additional seepage
pathways as it matures. In addition, grassy vegetation should be maintained to a
reasonable height on a periodic basis to allow for continuous unobstructed visual
observation of the embankments. On the day of the inspection, the grassy
vegetation was long and matted in sections at the right embankment, directly
impacting visual observations. PacifiCorp should review its current vegetation
management procedures to ensure woody vegetation and long grass are
discouraged from being established.
3. As documented in previous dam safety inspections, concrete deterioration was
observed at several Bigfork project structures, e.g., the decommissioned fish
ladder, diversion dam, upper concrete flume, forebay, and ice chute. PacifiCorp
should continue to prioritize repairs at these project structures to facilitate
continued safe access for operations staff and minimize the potential for a
prolonged outage.
4. Based on discussion with Mr. Kocaj, it is our understanding PacifiCorp is in the
early planning stages to make concrete repairs to an isolated location of the upper
concrete box flume. Based on our observations and recent incidents, we concur
with PacifiCorp prioritizing repairs to this area. We also encourage PacifiCorp to
make additional repairs to areas along the north side of the upper concrete box
flume that are significantly deteriorated and where vegetation was observed to be
established in a deteriorated pocket.
5. We observed a void near the interface of the buried HDPE flowline and forebay.
At the time of the inspection, there was no standing water or evidence of soft
material around the edges or in the interior of the void when probed. PacifiCorp
should further investigate this area to determine the extent of the void and provide
a repair plan to fix this area.
6. As documented in previous inspections, woody vegetation (trees) was observed to
be growing along the restored slope adjacent to the lower concrete flume. The
woody vegetation growing in the restored slope area should be controlled or
removed.
Please note that if we identify any additional items requiring follow-up action
during preparation of our Dam Safety Inspection Report, we will contact you by phone
and/or email and subsequently issue another letter.

3
Within 60 days of the date of this letter, please respond to or submit a plan and
schedule to address the comments above. File your submittal using the Commission’s
eFiling system at https://www.ferc.gov/ferc-online/overview. When eFiling, select
Hydro: Dam Safety and Portland Regional Office from the eFiling menu. The cover page
of the filing must indicate that the material was eFiled. For assistance with eFiling,
contact FERC Online Support at FERCOnlineSupport@ferc.gov, (866) 208-3676 (toll
free), or (202) 502-8659 (TTY).
Thank you for your continued cooperation and interest in dam safety. If you have
any questions, please contact Mr. Kareem Bynoe of this office at (503) 552-2719.
Sincerely,
Eric Kennedy, P.E.
Regional Engineer
